- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.3) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% relative to prior peak.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots in next 5–7 days; apply downward correction of 1–3% to avoid overreaction.
- If sentiment turns positive (avg > 0.1) after a downtrend, model frequently underreacts; increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% to capture sentiment-driven rebound.
- Model underestimates true price when sentiment is volatile (±0.3 or more in 3 consecutive days); apply +0.5–1.5% bias to forecast.
- For 30-day horizon, model often lags by 1–3 days in capturing sentiment-driven momentum; adjust forecast to align with sentiment peak 1–2 days ahead.
- When sentiment is negative and price is rising, model tends to ignore sentiment; if sentiment > -0.2 and price > 75, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% to reflect sentiment drag.
- If sentiment is negative and price is falling, model often overcorrects; if sentiment < -0.4 and price < 70, reduce forecast by 1–2% to avoid overcorrection.
